item.title: Trump calls AI fears a 'hoax' as tech exec warns of 'unseen hand' in regulation push
item.description:
## Google DeepMind researcher steps down, warning AI has potential to 'kill us all' Bilal Chughtai, who resigned from the [Google-owned AI lab](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) in July 2026 after working on AGI safety and alignment, said "we might be running out of time to avoid" the threat of being killed by AI.
## David Sacks says China’s AI optimism gives it an edge over US Entrepreneur David Sacks said optimism is the one area where China beats out the U.S., warning that it is the biggest risk to winning the [AI race](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) against China.
## Antony Blinken says AI has potential for 'extraordinary good' and 'catastrophic consequences' Secretary of State Antony Blinken said [AI has the potential](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) for "extraordinary good, but also for catastrophic consequences" if its development outpaces human ability to put necessary guardrails in place.
## Pentagon fires back at AI ‘doomers,’ vows US will remain dominant The new frontier of artificial intelligence belongs to us, not doomers.
The Pentagon’s technology office pushed back against calls to slow artificial intelligence development, declaring that the United States will control the technology’s next chapter.
“The new frontier of artificial intelligence belongs to us, not doomers,” the Department of War CTO wrote on X.

item.title: Pressure mounts on Congress to act on AI as UK warns of 'huge risk' without safety measures
item.description: # edigitalsurvey.com is blocked ## LIVE stream page 1 15. ![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2026/5/7/c3710b06-1ffa-4699-bd05-62077f19d9b7.jpg.webp)**Freya Scott-Turner** Live reporter Don't know your Grok from your Claude? The artificial intelligence sector is crowded with different players. Here's a non-exhaustive look at some of the key names to know. The main rivals are two companies that specialise in the development of AI models. These are **OpenAI** and **Anthropic.** OpenAI was founded in 2015. It's the firm behind **ChatGPT** and is headed up by Sam Altman. Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former employees of OpenAI who left the company after disagreements over vision and safety. It's the company behind AI assistant **Claude.** Elon Muskis another significant AI player. He's developed the chatbotGrok under his company SpaceXAI. And other major tech companies are also developing their own artificial intelligence. **Google** has its DeepMind laboratory, and **Meta** has built a virtual assistant, Meta AI. Share close panel Share page Copy link [About sharing](https://www.bbc.co.uk/usingthebbc/terms/can-i-share-things-from-the-bbc) 16. ![Louise Haigh](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/9/15/6fad5b4e-e7de-4488-96ac-6a85870409b9.jpg.webp)Image source, PA Media Across the Atlantic, the UK government has raised similar fears about the impact artificial intelligence could have if its development is left unchecked. Earlier today, First Secretary of State Louise Haigh - Prime Minister Andy Burnham's de facto deputy - said AI poses "huge risks" to the country's national security and society without the right protections. As a result, she said the UK needs to "heed the warnings" of those "at the forefront" of developing the technology and work with international partners to prioritise public safety - even if AI has "immense potential to improve lives". Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds, though, suggested the government should not be "hyperbolic" about the risks of AI, but accepted they should not be complacent. At the start of the week, a cross-party group of MPs and House of Lords peers published a report calling for a new law on AI to "address the scale and seriousness" of its threats. "Nowhere in the world, including the UK, has a current legislative and regulatory approach to AI that is fit for purpose," said Labour MP and committee chair Alex Sobel. ## [Rebel Democrats again help House GOP advance floor agenda](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/15/golden-gluesenkamp-perez-rule-vote-01078189) Two Senate Republicans said Tuesday that providing antitrust exemptions to artificial intelligence companies to facilitate discussions on how to make AI safer should be taken off the table — as lawmakers discuss ways to respond to industry warnings about the need for guardrails on the rapidly evolving technology.
Sen. [Bernie Sanders](https://directory.politicopro.com/congress/member/60c3186f-cbc6-4a13-90b4-7c3cb5e0567c) decried Washington on Tuesday for failing to regulate artificial intelligence, including the advanced models that AI researchers, tech executives and safety advocates warn pose an existential risk to humanity.
The Republican cosponsor of bipartisan artificial intelligence safety legislation said he sat down with OpenAI’s top lobbyist a day before the company backed a key provision in the bill that’s struggled to gain traction on Capitol Hill.
Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed fears of civilizational wipeout from artificial intelligence, comparing the recent alarms from inside AI labs to what he characterized as overblown warnings on the political left over climate change.
He did not address the topic that has dominated conversations in Congress in recent days: the risk posed by artificial intelligence and what, if anything, lawmakers ought to do about it.

item.title: Democrats are alarmed about AI. They’re not planning to hit it hard on the campaign trail.
item.description:
# Democrats are alarmed about AI. They’re not planning to hit it hard on the campaign trail. ## Share Other Democrats similarly want to keep hammering Republicans where they’re weakest — the economy — and worry that a last-minute pivot to focus on possible existential threats from artificial intelligence could prove a distraction from the issue voters have made clear they care about the most, according to a dozen Democratic lawmakers, pollsters and strategists.
Public opinion on artificial intelligence itself is “not as ripe or fully formed” as on data centers, which makes the latter a much more compelling argument for voters in the last stretch of the midterms, said Brad Bannon, a Democratic pollster and strategist.
Sixty percent of voters in a new Navigator Research poll selected inflation and cost of living as a top priority for the president and Congress to focus on, while only 16 percent selected artificial intelligence, according to the nationwide survey conducted by the Democratic firm Global Strategy Group Sept. 10-14 and shared first with POLITICO.
